entities.summary: Zhao Feiyan, formally Empress Xiaocheng (孝成皇后), was a Chinese courtesan and empress. She was an empress during the Han dynasty. Her husband was Emperor Cheng. She was known in the collective consciousness of Chinese society more for her beauty than for the regal presence that she and her sister, the Consort Zhao Hede engaged in and exuded, but unlike most of the famous beauties in Chinese history, she was often vilified by her own sisters. She was often contrasted with Yang Guifei, the concubine of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, because she was known for her slender build while Yang was known for her full build.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent empress of the Han dynasty, Empress Zhao Feiyan's beauty and influence played a significant role in shaping Chinese court politics during her reign. Her legacy serves as a reminder of the complex dynamics between women in power and their impact on imperial succession.
